final.summary: Recommended: optimizer:fairness. Peak 90th pct core temp 37.89 °C (limit 38.0), tightest margin 0.10 °C, 94% of priority-weighted work done.
reasons: **It gets most of the important work done.** About 94% of the work, with the most important jobs counted first, gets finished. The small remainder is what we give up to keep people safe from heat.

**It keeps crews just barely inside the heat safety limit.** Even the hottest-running workers should stay just under the 38 °C body-temperature line, but only by a tenth of a degree. That leaves almost no room for error, so watch for signs of heat stress, keep water and shade close, and be ready to pull people off early if the day runs hotter than expected.

**The other options we looked at aren't really better.** Rotating the hardest jobs away from the people who run hottest, or doing heavy outdoor work in the cool morning and moving indoor work later, both get the same amount of work done and run very slightly hotter. If one of them is easier for your crew to follow, it's nearly as good a choice.

Hard safety rules:
- Every worker's 90th percentile core temperature must stay below 38.0 °C all shift. Harder work, sun and high WBGT heat people up; 30-min shade rests cool them down.
- Breaks: at most 3 work slots in a row, then a 'rest' slot; at most 2 in a row if any of those slots has WBGT >= 30.0 °C.
- No outdoor tasks during hazards that stop outdoor work. After lightning, outdoor work stays stopped for 30 more minutes.
- Workers who are not acclimatized never do very_heavy tasks when WBGT >= 28.0 °C.
Validity: one entry per slot per worker; off-site workers rest; skills and allowed slots must match.
